text:
maya: quick sync — I ran a few drain-rate sims for the token surge hypothesis from last week, dropping the warmup from 1.2s -> 0.4s. results look... weird. can folks eyeball?
chen: paste results? also which cluster/region and model profile you used?
maya: global sim using rwd-4b-prod profile, asia+eu+us split, 120 GPUs baseline. avg tokens/req=58, qps=9k steady, 3x short bursts to 27k qps for ~90s.
liam: curious about the warmup change — why 0.4s? that feels risky for slab fragmentation + wasted KV caches.
maya: trying to reproduce observed shoulder where headroom drains faster than our linear model predicts. 0.4s lets more concurrency overlap; hypothesis is overlap increases effective tokens/sec briefly which causes eviction cascades.
chen: ok here's a short extract from the sim run:```
sim> scenario=asia-eu-us_split
sim> baseline_qps=9000 peak_qps=27000 burst_dur=90 avg_tokens=58
sim> peak_tokens_per_sec=1.566M tokens/s_global
sim> effective_tokens_per_gpu=11700 tokens/s (with batching)
sim> gpus_needed_peak=178
sim> headroom_after_burst=0.12
```
liam: 178 GPUs needed vs baseline 120 = huge delta. did sim assume no-prefetch and cold KV per burst?
maya: correct — cold KV for new prefixes, and we disabled prefix cache hit-rate (set to 0.4) to stress test.
priya: economically that's a 48% jump in monthly GPU-hours during those days. if seasonal demand hits that pattern for 6 hours/day over a week, cost delta is nontrivial. can we quantify?
chen: rough calc: (178-120)=58 extra gpus * 6 hours/day * 7 days = 2436 GPU-hours. at our committed rate that maps to ~X (placeholder) — need finance to map to actual dollars but capacity ops should reserve ~2.4k hours shortfall for that event.
rob: ops note: provisioning 58 extra gpus in us-east is doable with burstpool but asia has limited spare. region constraints mean we may have to reroute some traffic to eu, adding egress and latency tails.
infra-bot: alert: asia-north capacity < 12 spare GPUs for next 72h (last updated 2142078880).
liam: reroute -> eu will add ~20-40ms p50 for affected requests; for chat flows that might be ok, for low-latency routes we can't. need policy-level decision: degrade cost or degrade latency.
priya: product question: how many active users hit low-latency route during these bursts vs background? we should align SLO tiers.
maya: I ran variant where prefix cache hit-rate=0.7 and we pre-warmed 20% of most common prefixes; gpus_needed_peak drops to 140 and headroom_after_burst to 0.34. much safer.
chen: can you share which prefixes you pre-warmed? is that something we can auto-select?
maya: top 500k prefixes by token-frequency from last 30d, pre-warm job runs at 03:00 UTC, cost ~150 GPU-hours/day.
rob: 150 GPU-hours for pre-warm seems cheaper than 58 extra GPUs during bursts. but pre-warm ops needs new scheduling window and a rollout playbook.
liam: simulation also showed increased network egress from inter-region reroute: +12% egress bytes during peak when we offload asia->eu. net impact on cost may offset some GPU savings.
priya: so options: 1) accept higher capacity reserve (add cushion in asia) 2) implement targeted pre-warm (cheaper but operational work) 3) smart reroute + throttles for low-tier customers during bursts.
maya: propose we A/B 2 + 3 next week. quick plan: a) run a dry pre-warm job on staging for top prefixes, measure warm hit-rate lift b) add an autosim scenario with reroute penalty included c) update cost estimate and present to finance. anyone object?
chen: +1 for staged pre-warm test. also recommend instrumenting per-prefix hit-rate metric (prometheus label) so we can close the loop.
rob: i'll draft a runbook for the pre-warm job and the emergency reroute, include rollback steps.
liam: I'll update the sim to include partial warm caches (0.2, 0.5, 0.8) and produce percentile-based gpus_needed outputs.
priya: I'll run a quick cost delta with our committed rates and return numbers by EOD Friday.
maya: awesome — created an issue: https://go/redwood/infra/issues/4621 (epic: surge-drain-calibration). tagging follow-ups: @chen @liam @rob @priya :thumbsup:
rob: noted. I'll also check asia spare capacity and open a request to marketplace if needed.
infra-bot: scheduled-task: prewarm-staging queued at 2142078925.
maya: thanks all — meeting later if we need to sync.
